The clause «إنّه لحقّ» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.
The clause «ما أنتم بمعجزين» has no grammatical position, being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the answer to the oath.

* Benefits:
- «إي» with kasra and sukūn:
In this verse there occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ, where (إي) is a particle of answer. We will set out what Ibn Hishām related about it:
It is a particle of answer meaning «نعم» (yes), so it serves to confirm the one who informs, to inform the one who asks, and to promise the one who requests; so it occurs after: «قام زيد» (Zayd stood), «هل قام زيد» (did Zayd stand?), «اضرب زيدا» (strike Zayd) and the like, just as «نعم» occurs after them. Ibn al-Ḥājib claimed that it occurs after the interrogative, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّي إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ, and according to all of them it occurs only before an oath, as in the verse «إِي وَرَبِّي». [Translator's note: in Ibn Hishām's Mughnī, Ibn al-Ḥājib's claim is that it occurs only after the interrogative; the source here does not include the word «إنما» (only).]

safi-cedvel:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لو) non-jussive conditional particle; (أنّ) particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh); (لكلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted khabar (predicate); (نفس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (ظلمت) past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and the fāʿil (agent) is «هي», i.e. every soul; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the postponed noun of anna; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما».
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لكلّ ... ما في الأرض) is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being «ثبت» (it were established), i.e. the existence [of ...] were established..
(اللام) occurring in the apodosis of «لو»; (افتدت) like «ظلمت»; (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (افتدت); (الواو) conjunctive; (أسرّوا) past verb with its fāʿil; (الندامة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (لمّا) adverb meaning «حين» (when), containing the meaning of condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to the implied apodosis; (رأوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (العذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunctive; (قضي ... لا يظلمون) its i'rab has already passed [Note: in verse (47) of this sūra.].
The clause «(ثبت) امتلاك ما في الأرض» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ظلمت ...» is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «نفس».
The clause «افتدت» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أسرّوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause [Note: or resumptive, if the concealing takes place in the Hereafter.].
The clause «رأوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.
The clause «قضي بينهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هم لا يظلمون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «لا يظلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).

safi-cedvel:55-55.t:
* I'rab:
(ألا) particle of alerting (tanbīh); (إنّ) particle resembling the verb; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted khabar (predicate); (ما) relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [word], the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (الواو) conjunctive; (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «السموات», genitive (majrūr); (ألا إنّ) like the first; (وعد) noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (الله) the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (حقّ) khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) conjunctive; (لكنّ) like «إنّ»; (أكثر) noun of lākinna, accusative, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negative; (يعلمون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
The clause «إنّ لله ما في السموات» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ أكثرهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «إنّ وعد الله حقّ».
The clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

safi-cedvel:56-56.t:
* I'rab:
(هو) detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يحيي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is «هو»; (الواو) conjunctive; (يميت) like «يحيي»; (الواو) conjunctive; (إلى) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترجعون), which is an imperfect verb, passive, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «هو يحيي ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحيي ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ «هو».
The clause «يميت ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the khabar clause.
The clause «ترجعون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:57-57.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a specified indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative, and (ها) is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الناس) badal (substitute) of «أيّ», following it in the nominative in form — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); (قد) particle of verification (taḥqīq); (جاءت) past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (موعظة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «موعظة» [Note: or attached to (جاءتكم) if (من) is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).. and the construction is figurative.], and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunctive; (شفاء) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «موعظة», nominative; (اللام) preposition; (ما) relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt of «شفاء» [Note: this is if (شفاء) is a noun meaning «دواء» (remedy).. and if it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), then (اللام) is redundant (zāʾida), for strengthening, and (ما) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of «شفاء».]; (في الصدور) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted [word], the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (الواو) conjunctive in both places; (هدى، رحمة) two nouns conjoined by the two conjunctions to «موعظة», nominative, the sign of the nominative in (هدى) being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (للمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «رحمة», the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «the vocative يأيّها ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «جاءتكم موعظة ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.

* Morphology:
(شفاء): a transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb «شفى يشفي», of the pattern-class «ضرب»; it was then made into a descriptive for intensiveness, or it is a noun for that which heals, like «الدواء» (medicine). Its pattern is «فعال» with kasra on the fāʾ. It contains iʿlāl or ibdāl (substitution) by changing the weak letter into a hamza; its original form is «شفاي», and when the yāʾ came at the end after a quiescent alif it was changed into a hamza.

* Benefits:
In this verse there occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted قَدْ جاءَتْكُمْ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَشِفاءٌ لِما فِي الصُّدُورِ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ. Here we are concerned with the noun (هدى): it is conjoined to «موعظة» and nominative like it, by the ḍamma implied on the alif, which is dropped in pronunciation because of the tanwīn but kept in writing. Someone might imagine that the tanwīn on the alif is a case vowel, but it is not so; rather, it is an indication of the dropped alif. To clarify this point we say: when the maqṣūr noun (the noun ending in alif) is devoid of definition by «أل» and devoid of annexation (iḍāfa), it takes tanwīn in all cases of i'rab, and the vowels are implied on its alif, which is dropped because of the tanwīn. It is known that this alif is dropped in pronunciation and kept in writing, but in i'rab we consider it dropped. If, however, the maqṣūr noun does not take tanwīn — that being when it comes annexed (muḍāf) or defined by «أل» — then we parse it with vowels implied on the alif, whose appearance is prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur).

safi-cedvel:90-92.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (جاوزنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn..
and (نا) a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). (ببني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جاوزنا) [Note: The bāʾ here is for transitivity (taʿdiya), i.e.: We made the Children of Israel cross the sea.], and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, as it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa. (البحر) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الفاء) conjunction. (أتبع) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (فرعون) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and it is barred from nunation because of being a proper name and foreign. (جنود) conjoined to فرعون by the wāw, nominative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (بغيا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: Or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "transgressing".], (عدوا) conjoined to (بغيا) by the wāw, accusative. (حتى) a particle of inception (ibtidāʾ). (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (قال), (أدرك) a past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الغرق) fāʿil, nominative. (قال) like أدرك, and the fāʿil is "he". (آمنت) a past verb and its fāʿil. (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, abrogating (nāsikh) — for emphasis — and (الهاء) the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), in the position of accusative as the noun of anna. (لا) the lā of generic negation. (إله) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative, and the khabar (predicate) of lā is omitted, its implied form being "existent" or "worshipped in truth". (إلّا) a particle of exception. (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as badal (substitute) from the pronoun latent in the khabar [Note: It is parsed as badal because the clause before the particle of exception is negated.. And the relative may be in the position of accusative as excepted.] (آمنت) a past verb.. and (التاء) for the feminine. (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (آمنت), (بنو) fāʿil, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw, as it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. (إسرائيل) like the first.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه لا إله ...) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (آمنت), i.e.: "I believed in that there is no god except ...".
(الواو) conjunction. (أنا) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (من المسلمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «جاوزنا ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أتبعهم فرعون ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause جاوزنا.
The clause «أدركه الغرق» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position; apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «آمنت ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «لا إله إلّا ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of anna.
The clause «آمنت به بنو ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أنا من المسلمين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
(الهمزة) for reproachful interrogation. (الآن) an adverb of time, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being تؤمن ("do you believe"). (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl. (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq). (عصيت) like آمنت. (قبل) an adverb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (عصيت), (الواو) conjunction. (كنت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb.. and (التاء) a pronoun, the noun of kāna, in the position of nominative. (من المفسدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of kāna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «(تؤمن) الآن ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl of an implied saying, which is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «قد عصيت» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the fāʿil in (تؤمن).
The clause «كنت من المفسدين» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.
(الفاء) conjunction. (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (ننجيك), which is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.. and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن" (We), for majesty. (ببدن) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the pronoun of address, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام) for cause (taʿlīl). (تكون) an incomplete imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you). (اللام) a preposition. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to a ḥāl from آية — a naʿt (adjective) placed before the noun it qualifies — (آية) khabar of takūn, accusative. And (خلف) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of من, and (الكاف) like the last.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (ننجيك).
(الواو) parenthetical. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — abrogating — (كثيرا) the noun of inna, accusative. (من الناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt of (كثيرا), (عن آيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (غافلون), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام) it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis. (غافلون) khabar of inna, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «ننجيك ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «تكون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ كثيرا من الناس ...» has no grammatical position; a parenthetical tail-clause (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī) to confirm the reported speech.

* Morphology:
(الغرق), an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb غرق يغرق, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
Double entendre (al-tawriya): in His saying, Exalted is He, «فَالْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ», if بدن is interpreted as the coat of mail. But if it is interpreted as the body, the meaning is: We shall save you in the state in which there is no spirit in you, and you are only a body. As for interpreting بدن as the coat of mail, the saying of ʿAmr ibn Maʿdī Karib indicates it:
أعاذل شكّتي بدني وسيفي ... وكلّ مقلّص سلس القياد
(O you who reproach me, my weapons are my coat of mail and my sword, and every lean, tightly-girthed horse, easy to lead.)
Pharaoh had a coat of mail of gold by which he was known, and so tawriya is valid in البدن: in its near, apparent sense, البدن means the body, and in its far, hidden sense it means the coat of mail, and the hidden sense is the one intended; for Pharaoh's being saved — i.e. his coming out of the sea after drowning — with his coat of mail is a more wondrous sign than his coming out bare. Tawriya, briefly, is: that the speaker mentions a single word that has two meanings: a near, apparent one that is not intended, and a far, hidden one that is the intended one.

safi-cedvel:93-93.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (اللام) the lām of oath, for an implied oath. (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq). (بوأنا) like جاوزنا «1», (بني) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ. (إسرائيل) like the previous one «2», (مبوّأ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: By making (بوّأ) contain the sense of أنزل ("to lodge").. And it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), on the basis that it is a mīmī maṣdar..
Or it is an adverb attached to (بوّأنا), on the basis that it is a noun of place.], (صدق) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (رزقنا) like جاوزنا «4», and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (من الطيّبات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (رزقنا). (الفاء) conjunction. (ما) negative. (اختلفوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (حتى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. (جاء) a past verb, and (هم) like the last. (العلم) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (إنّ ربّ) like إنّ كثيرا [Note: In verse (92) of this sūra.], and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يقضي) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "he". (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يقضي), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يقضي), (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (في) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (يقضي), (كانوا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (في) like the first, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يختلفون), which is an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil. The interpreted maṣdar (أن جاءهم) is in the position of genitive, attached to (اختلفوا).
The clause «بوّأنا ...» has no grammatical position; response to an implied oath.
The clause «رزقناهم..» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause of the response to the oath.
The clause «ما اختلفوا ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause رزقناهم.
The clause «جاءهم العلم» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ ربك يقضي ...» has no grammatical position; an explanatory resumptive clause.
The clause «يقضي ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «كانوا فيه يختلفون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يختلفون» is in the position of accusative as khabar of kānū.

* Morphology:
(مبوّأ), a mīmī maṣdar (verbal noun) — or a noun of place — and it is valid to take both considerations in the verse.. Its pattern is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:94-94.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (إن) a conditional particle that makes jussive. (كنت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (التاء) is the noun of kāna. (في شكّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of kunta. (من) a preposition. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of شكّ. (أنزلنا) like جاوزنا [Note: In verse (90) of this sūra.
(2, 3) in the previous verse (93).], (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزلنا), (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اسأل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (يقرءون) like يختلفون «2», (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقرءون), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لقد جاء) like بوّأنا, indeclinable on the fatḥa «3», and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الحقّ) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاء). (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تكوننّ) an incomplete imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive ... and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you). (من الممترين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of takūnanna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «كنت في شكّ....» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أنزلنا» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «اسأل ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يقرءون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «جاءك الحقّ ...» has no grammatical position; response to an implied oath.
The clause «لا تكوننّ من الممترين» has no grammatical position; apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you have grasped it, then do not be ...".

* Benefits:
Does the Messenger of Allah ﷺ doubt what was sent down to him? Regarding this verse a question and an objection have been raised. It is to say: did the Prophet ﷺ doubt what was sent down to him concerning his prophethood, so that he should ask?
And if he were doubtful of his own prophethood, others would be more worthy of doubt than him. The answer to this question is what al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ said in his book al-Shifāʾ: "Beware — may Allah make your heart firm — lest there occur to your mind what some exegetes have mentioned from Ibn ʿAbbās or others, of affirming this doubt of the Prophet ﷺ — regarding what was revealed to him — on the ground that he is a human being; for the like of this is not possible for him ﷺ at all. Rather, Ibn ʿAbbās said: The Prophet ﷺ did not doubt, and did not ask. And similar is reported from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī.
And it is related from Qatāda that he said: It has reached us that the Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the source has «صلّى عليه وآله وسلم», with the word «الله» missing] said, when this verse was revealed: I do not doubt and I do not ask. And the generality of the exegetes hold this." The speech of al-Qāḍī ʿIyāḍ, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, ends here. Then they differed regarding the meaning of the verse and who is addressed, holding two views. One of them is that the address is to the Prophet ﷺ outwardly, while someone else is meant by it; so it is like His saying (لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ), and it is known that the Prophet ﷺ did not associate partners, so it is established that someone else is meant by it.
And among the proverbs of the Arabs is «إياك أعني واسمعي يا جارة» ("It is you I mean, but listen, O neighbour-woman"). What indicates the soundness of this interpretation is His saying, Exalted is He, at the end of this sūra: قُلْ يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ دِينِي. And it has been said: Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, knew that the Prophet ﷺ never doubted at all, so what is meant by this is stirring him up (al-tahyīj); for when he ﷺ heard this speech he would say: I do not doubt, O Lord, and I do not ask. And al-Zajjāj said that Allah addressed the Messenger ﷺ in His saying (فإن كنت في شك), while it encompasses all of creation; so it is like His saying يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ. This is a good approach. But there is remoteness in it, because the Prophet ﷺ is included in this address and the objection remains standing. The other view is that this address is not to the Prophet ﷺ at all. The rationale of this view is that people in his time were three groups: one believing him, one belying him, and one doubting; so the Exalted addressed the third group with this speech, and Allah knows best.
And they differed regarding those to be asked in His saying, Exalted is He, in this verse, فَسْئَلِ الَّذِينَ يَقْرَؤُنَ الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ. The meticulous scholars among the people of exegesis said: they are those of the People of the Book who believed, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions, because they are the ones whose reports are trusted.

safi-cedvel:95-95.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (لا تكونن) like the previous one «1», (من) a preposition. (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of takūnanna. (كذّبوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كذّبوا), (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya). (تكون) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the fāʾ, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you). (من الخاسرين) like من الممترين «2».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكون) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding النبي [Translator's note: so in the source; «النهي» (the prohibition) is evidently meant], i.e. "let there not be from you a belying of the signs of Allah, and so loss".
The clause «لا تكوننّ ...» is conjoined to the clause لا تكوننّ من الممترين «3». [Translator's note: the source does not state the clause's position here.]
The clause «كذّبوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «تكون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).

safi-cedvel:96-98.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb. (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (حقّت) a past verb.. and (التاء) for the feminine. (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حقّت), (كلمة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (ربّ) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (الكاف) in the position of genitive by annexation. (لا) negative. (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil.
The clause «إنّ الذين حقّت ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «حقّت.. كلمة....» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يؤمنون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna.
(الواو) the wāw of ḥāl. (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (جاءت) like حقّت, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (كلّ) fāʿil, nominative. (آية) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (حتى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. (يروا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn..
and the wāw is fāʿil. (العذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الأليم) naʿt (adjective) of العذاب, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يروا) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (لا يؤمنون).
The clause «جاءتهم كلّ آية ...» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يؤمنون..
And the apodosis (jawāb) of law is omitted, what precedes it indicating it.
The clause «يروا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
(الفاء) conjunction. (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) in the sense of هلّا, containing the sense of reproach. (كانت) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb [Note: Or complete (tāmm), its fāʿil being (قرية), and the clause آمنت a naʿt of قرية.. And the word قرية is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) by which its inhabitants are meant.] and (التاء) for the feminine. (قرية) the noun of kānat, nominative. (آمنت) like حقّت [Note: In verse (96) of this sūra.], (الفاء) conjunction. (نفع) a past verb, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (إيمان) fāʿil, nominative, and (ها) muḍāf ilayhi. (إلّا) a particle of exception. (قوم) excepted, accusative [Note: It has been said: the exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), because the people are not of the genus of the town.. And it has been said: rather it is joined (muttaṣil), because by the town its inhabitants are meant.] (يونس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa. (لما) an adverb in the sense of "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (كشفنا), (آمنوا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (كشفنا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (عن) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (كشفنا), (عذاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الخزي) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (في الحياة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عذاب [Note: Or to a ḥāl from it.], (الدنيا) naʿt of الحياة, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (الواو) conjunction. (متّعنا) like كشفنا, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (إلى حين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (متّعناهم).
The clause «لولا كانت قرية ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause.
The clause «آمنت ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of kānat [Note: Or it is a naʿt of قرية, and the clause نفعها إيمانها is the khabar of kānat, with the fāʾ being redundant in the khabar.].
The clause «نفعها إيمانها» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause آمنت.
The clause «آمنوا ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كشفنا ...» has no grammatical position; apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «متّعناهم ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the apodosis clause.

* Morphology:
(يونس), a foreign name. In Lisān al-ʿArab it comes: «يونس — with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the nūn — three dialectal forms — the name of a man, and the hamza has also been reported in it.» End of quote.

* Benefits:
- The inimitability of the Qur'an:
In these two verses there is one of the aspects of the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, for He affirms in them:
that those against whom the word of disbelief has come due will never believe, and will not acknowledge the truth of Islam until they see the painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection. The aspect of inimitability is that we see with our own eyes a group of people who persist in disbelief and go deep in it, and who never believe, however much proof, evidence and persuasion you make clear to them; and they remain insistent on disbelief, such that even if you showed them Allah openly they would say: this is sorcery and falsehood. This group is not particular to one time rather than another; rather it has existed from the time of Adam and his offspring until the coming of the Hour. So if you see a person persisting in disbelief and never being convinced of Islam, which is the truth, this is a proof of the truthfulness of the Noble Qur'an, and that it is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, who created man and knows what he is upon.
- Mention of the story of the people of Yūnus:
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Wahb and others mentioned it. They said: The people of Yūnus were in the town of Nineveh, in the land of Mosul, and they were people of disbelief and polytheism. So Allah, Glorified is He, sent to them Yūnus, upon him be blessing and peace, calling them to belief in Allah, but they refused him. So it was said to him: Tell them that the punishment will come upon them in the morning within three days. He told them that, and they said: We have never found him to lie, so watch: if he spends the night among you tonight, then it is nothing; but if he does not spend the night, then know that the punishment will come upon you in the morning. When it was the middle of the night, Yūnus went out from among them, and when they woke in the morning the punishment covered them, and it was above their heads. Ibn ʿAbbās said: The punishment had been sent down upon the people of Yūnus until there was between them and it only the measure of two-thirds of a mile; then when they supplicated, Allah removed that from them. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: The punishment covered the people of Yūnus as the garment covers the grave. And Wahb said: When the punishment covered them, they went out with their children, their livestock and their women to the open desert, put on sackcloth, and proclaimed Islam and repentance, and they were sincere; so their Lord had mercy on them, answered their supplication, and removed from them what had descended upon them. This is of Allah's great mercy to His servants, and that He accepts repentance and pardons evil deeds, and does not pour out the whip of His punishment except upon a people whose belief is not hoped for.
- In this verse occurs His saying, Exalted is He, فَلَوْلا كانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَها إِيمانُها إِلَّا قَوْمَ يُونُسَ. Views have been put forward about (لولا) in this verse, and Ibn Hishām spoke on this topic, saying: "Al-Harawī mentioned that لولا can be negative, in the status of لم, and he counted among such the (لولا) occurring in this verse. But what is apparent is that the meaning is one of reproach, i.e. 'why was there not a single town among the destroyed towns that turned back [Translator's note: the source has «ثابت», evidently for «تابت» (repented)] from disbelief before the coming of the punishment, so that that benefited it?' This is the interpretation of al-Akhfash, al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ, ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā and al-Naḥḥās, and it is supported by the reading of Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh (فهلّا كانت). Negation follows necessarily from this meaning, because reproach entails non-occurrence. It may be imagined that al-Zamakhsharī holds that it is for negation, because of his saying: 'The exception is disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), in the sense of لكن ("but"), and it may be joined (muttaṣil), the clause being in the sense of negation, as though it were said: "no [town] believed"'; but perhaps he only meant what we have mentioned, and for this reason he said: 'and the clause is in the sense of negation', and did not say: 'and لولا is for negation'. The Seven (i.e. the readers) agreed on the accusative in (إلا قوم), which indicates that the speech is affirmative (mūjab), but there is in it a scent of non-affirmation, like the saying of al-Akhṭal:
وبالصريمة منزل منزل خلق ... عاف تغيّر إلا النؤي والوتد
(And at al-Ṣarīma there is a worn-out dwelling, effaced, changed, all but the trench and the tent-peg.) [Translator's note: the source repeats «منزل»; the verse is usually cited as «وبالصريمة منهم منزل خلق».]
عاف: effaced (ruined). النؤي: a trench around the tent that keeps water from it. In this verse there is a scent of negation, because تغيّر means 'did not remain as it was'."

safi-cedvel:99-100.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive. (لو شاء) like لو جاء [Note: In verse (97) of this sūra.], (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (اللام) linking the apodosis (jawāb) of law. (آمن) a past verb. (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من. (كلّ) semantic tawkīd (emphasis) of the relative noun, following it in the nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (جميعا) an emphasizing ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, accusative (manṣūb). (الهمزة) for interrogation. (الفاء) conjunction. (أنت) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or the fāʿil of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned, in the manner of ishtighāl, i.e.: "will you (أنت) compel the people ...". That is because the interrogative hamza is more closely attached to the verb than to the noun.], (تكره) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "you". (الناس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (حتّى) a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. (يكونوا) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى.. and the wāw is a pronoun, the noun of kāna. (مؤمنين) khabar (predicate), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكونوا..) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (تكره).
The clause «لو شاء ربّك ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «آمن من في الأرض» has no grammatical position; apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أنت تكره ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تكره الناس ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنت.
The clause «يكونوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
(الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative. (كان) an incomplete past verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — [Note: It may be complete (tāmm), in the sense of "to be right" or "to be fitting", the fāʿil being the interpreted maṣdar.], (لنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, fronted khabar [Note: Or attached to the complete verb كان.], (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative. (تؤمن) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is "she".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تؤمن) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of kāna.
(إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the fāʿil of تؤمن, i.e. "except accompanied by the permission of Allah". (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
(الواو) conjunction. (يجعل) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he". (الرجس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (على) a preposition. (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi of the verb يجعل. (لا) negative. (يعقلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil.
The clause «ما كان لنفس ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause شاء ربّك.
The clause «تؤمن ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يجعل ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "so He permits some to believe, and makes ..." etc.
The clause «لا يعقلون» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذين).

safi-cedvel:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (انظروا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (ماذا) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: Or (ما) is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and (ذا) a relative noun, khabar (predicate), and (في السموات) the ṣila (relative clause).], (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (الواو) conjunction. (الأرض) conjoined to السموات, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) parenthetical. (ما) negative [Note: Or an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e.: "what avail"], (تغني) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, (الآيات) fāʿil, nominative. (الواو) conjunction. (النذر) conjoined to الآيات, nominative. (عن قوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تغني), (لا يؤمنون) like لا يعقلون [Note: In the previous verse (100).].
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «انظروا ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «ماذا في السموات ...» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
The clause «تغني الآيات» has no grammatical position; a parenthetical tail-clause (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī) to the preceding clause.
The clause «لا يؤمنون» is in the position of genitive as naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

safi-cedvel:102-102.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive. (ينتظرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is fāʿil (agent). And (هل) interrogative in the sense of negation. (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (مثل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (أيّام) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (الذين) a relative in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (خلوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلوا), and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (قل) like the earlier one «1», (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (انتظروا) like انظروا «2», (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to المنتظرين, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (من المنتظرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «هل ينتظرون ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive [Note: It may be in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied jussive condition, i.e.: "if the warnings do not avail them, then do they await anything but the like of the days of those who passed away (خلو) [Translator's note: so in the source, for «خلوا»]....?"].
The clause «خلوا ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «انتظروا ...» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you are awaiting that, then wait ...", and the clause of the condition and apodosis is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إنّي معكم من المنتظرين» has no grammatical position; it has the status of a causal (taʿlīliyya) clause.

safi-cedvel:103-103.t:
* I'rab:
(ثمّ) a conjunction. (ننجي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil (agent) is "We", for majesty. (رسل) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو) conjunction. (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined to رسل. (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (الكاف) a preposition. (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose governor is ننجي.. and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address. (حقّا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. حقّ ذلك حقّا ("that is truly due") [Note: It may be a badal (substitute) from the maṣdar to which (كذلك) is attached.], (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (حقّا), (ننجي) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ; the yāʾ has been dropped in the script of the Muṣḥaf because it fell away in pronunciation due to the meeting of two quiescents, and the fāʿil is "We", for majesty. (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «ننجي ...» is conjoined to implied speech, i.e.: "We destroy the nations, then We save Our messengers".
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «(حقّ) حقا..» has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «ننجي (the second)» has no grammatical position; resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
Representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): in His saying, Exalted is He, «كَذلِكَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا نُنْجِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ», i.e. "like that saving, We save the believers among you and destroy the polytheists". He likened the salvation of those believers who remain to the salvation of those who passed, and the point of resemblance is that each of them deserves salvation.

safi-cedvel:104-106.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you". (يا) a vocative particle. (أيّ) the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh). (الناس) badal (substitute) from أيّ — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — following it in the nominative in form. (أن) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has «إن»] a conditional particle that makes jussive. (كنتم) an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb — abrogating (nāsikh) — indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and the wāw is the noun of kāna. (في شكّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of kuntum. (من ديني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) شك, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on what precedes the yāʾ.. and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (لا) negative. (أعبد) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is "I". (الذين) a relative in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (تعبدون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is fāʿil. (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referential pronoun, i.e. "you worship it, being other than Allah". (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (الواو) conjunction. (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect. (أعبد الله) like أعبد الذين. (الذي) a relative in the position of accusative as naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty. (يتوفّى) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he". (الواو) conjunction. (أمرت) a passive past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء) is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle that makes accusative. (أكون) an incomplete imperfect verb — abrogating — and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (I). (من المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of akūna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (أمرت), i.e. "to be" (بأن أكون) [Note: The interpreted maṣdar may be a mafʿūl bihi of the verb أمرت.].
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «the vocative ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (object of speech).
The clause «إن كنتم في شك» has no grammatical position; response to the vocative.
The clause «لا أعبد ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «تعبدون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «أعبد الله» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا أعبد.
The clause «يتوفّاكم» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أمرت ...» is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا أعبد.
The clause «أكون ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
(الواو) conjunction. (أن) an explicative particle [Note: Or a maṣdar-forming particle, the interpreted maṣdar being the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb أوحي إليّ ("it was revealed to me"), or قيل لي ("it was said to me").] with an implied verb, i.e. "it was revealed to me that ...". (أقم) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". (وجه) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (للدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أقم), (حنيفا) ḥāl, accusative, from the pronoun of the fāʿil in أقم, or from الدين. (الواو) conjunction. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تكوننّ) an incomplete imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you). (من المشركين) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of takūnanna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «أقم ...» has no grammatical position; explicative.. and the implied clause "it was revealed to me".. is in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا أعبد ...
The clause «لا تكوننّ ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the explicative clause.
(الواو) conjunction. (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تدع) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is "you". (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the relative ما. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (لا) negative. (ينفع) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "you" [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʿil of ينفعك is a latent pronoun "it" referring to ما]. (الواو) conjunction. (لا يضرّك) like لا ينفعك, (الفاء) resumptive. (إن) a conditional particle that makes jussive. (فعلت) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis.. and (التاء) is fāʿil. (الفاء) linking the apodosis. (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (إذا) a particle of response with no governing effect. (من الظالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of inna, and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «لا تدع ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the clause أقم [Note: Or it is conjoined to the clause قل يأيّها الناس.. And it may be resumptive.].
The clause «لا ينفعك ...» has no grammatical position; ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «لا يضرّك» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «إن فعلت ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «إنّك.. من الظالمين» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(تدع), in it there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by dropping, owing to the jussive; its origin is تدعو, and its pattern is تفع.

* Benefits:
In this verse occurs His saying, Exalted is He, وَلكِنْ أَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ. Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, has brought the attribute of "taking in death" (al-tawaffī) in this verse, and we will present the wisdom of that as the exegetes stated it: What is meant is that the One who deserves worship, so that I and you should worship Him, is the One who created you first when you were nothing, then causes you to die second, then gives you life after death. So He sufficed with mentioning death as an alert to the rest, and that the One who gives life and causes death is more worthy of worship than any other. And it has been said: since death is the hardest of things on the soul, it was mentioned in this place so as to be stronger in restraint and deterrence. And it has been said: when they were hasty in demanding the punishment, He answered them with His saying: "but I worship Allah, who is able to destroy you and to grant me victory over you". This is of the inimitability of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and that there is no word but it has been placed in its proper place.
